signals.evidence: Avram Pechima, CEO of Eilat Hashchar kibbutz hotel, coordinates reception of displaced residents from rocket attacks; municipality representative Liat Chen manages support center for children whose homes were destroyed
Hotel staff receive displaced residents arriving at all hours, provide emotional support and ensure care for those whose homes were damaged by Hezbollah fire
Hotel operating as shelter for displaced residents; municipality support center functioning for children without homes
Nizari opened a coffee shop named 'Friendship' to commemorate fallen friends and honor the value of camaraderie that the state is built upon

Holocaust survivor Raya: 'I was at the bottom, I fought, I survived, I came to Israel and built a wonderful family, so there is hope to emerge from a very difficult period. I hope this will inspire them and give them hope'
Mother of fallen daughter: 'I see the capabilities of the Air Force in Iran and I think they could have saved my daughter. Where were these capabilities when my daughter was still alive?'

Mother: 'War with Iran causes pressure and distress. Every time I go down to the shelter during an alert, I call the children to see where they are and my heart shrinks: where is Osher? Osher is not here. Every alert I think about October 7'
Mother experiencing ongoing trauma and anxiety related to daughter's death and current war, triggered by alerts and reminders of October 7
Ella Yafrah, 19, pre-military program participant: 'I volunteer here every day. I help the shop owner pack shipments and run the business. When we saw the situation in the north, we came right away'
Shop in Kibbutz Amir operating with volunteer support despite ongoing war conditions
Pre-military program teaches: 'If we need a wheel, then I am a wheel. We help wherever needed. When we saw the situation in the north, we came right away'
Ramat Hasharon municipality decided not to open educational institutions today due to security alerts; will convene with education officials to develop safe plan for return to studies next week
Fallen munitions in Finger of Galilee caused damage to building in Mishgav Am; one person reported frightened
Ramat Hasharon closed educational institutions; Herzliya kept schools open under 'green' defense policy
Noa'a, 30, from Jerusalem: 'I felt I was dying of fear that an alert would catch me. Every such sound put me in terrible stress. I haven't left the house because I felt I was dying of fear'

Noa'a: 'Since October 7 I understood the world is a wild and dangerous place, surrounded by cruel enemies who want to destroy us. I have been in therapy since October 7, and during the war sessions were remote. I haven't left the house because I felt I was dying of fear'

Orit (pseudonym), mother of three from Tel Aviv area: 'I can count on one hand the number of times I left the house in the last month. The farthest I went was to the nearby shopping center because it has a protected space'

Orit: 'I understand war is dangerous and bad things can happen anywhere. But in the current situation where I have no control, I feel I can at least control staying close to the protected room. Fortunately, my workplace accepted that I work only remotely'

Wisam Saliman, tour guide from Galilee: 'War started on February 28, I had bookings for those dates - everything was cancelled. This is a loss of tens of thousands of shekels. I'm still paying loans from Corona. After October 7 I broke the rest of my savings. I took more loans, interest is choking me, and I'm delaying the end'
Tourism sites in Jaffa empty; fish market abandoned; restaurants empty; only shop owners with no work remain
Central Bureau of Statistics survey: 31% of small businesses in Israel had minimal employment or temporary closure during the war; approximately 220,000 small businesses closed since start of war

Home Front Command implemented early warning system for fire from north toward Ashdod; residents received advance warning 2.5 minutes before regular alert, providing total 3.25 minutes to reach protected spaces before missile impact

Yad2 platform data: demand for apartments with protected room (MAMAD) increased 3% since war start; demand for apartments without MAMAD fell 18%. In north, demand for non-MAMAD apartments fell 21.6%; in center 22%; in Jerusalem 19.5%
Health Ministry: 7,527 people admitted to hospitals with war-related injuries since February 28; 108 currently hospitalized (2 critical, 13 serious, 27 moderate, 66 good condition)
Energean resumed production at Karish gas field following Ministry of Energy decision to restore normal operations
